title: The Loaf and the Roll
story: The corner bakery had kept the same price for a plain loaf for two years. In March, Samir pinned a notice on the board saying that flour and energy cost more, so the loaf would cost a little more from Monday. A few regulars grumbled, and one said she might buy bread less often. Samir did not argue in the queue. The notice also promised that the smaller roll would stay the same price, so a tight budget still had an option. During the week he watched what people chose. Most still bought the loaf, and a few switched to the roll. On Friday the customer who had grumbled said the bread was worth the new price and bought her usual two loaves. Samir left the notice up for a month so the change could not be called a secret. He wrote both prices in his accounts in case costs fell later.

Power, such as electricity or gas, used to run something.

The amount of money a person can afford to spend.

quiz.question: What reason did the bakery give for the new loaf price?
options: Flour and the cost of running the ovens had risen
Customers had asked for a smaller roll only
The shop was closing on Monday
The old price had been kept secret for a month
quiz.correctAnswer: Flour and the cost of running the ovens had risen
quiz.explanation: The notice said flour and energy cost more, so the loaf would cost a little more.
quiz.supportingSentence: In March, Samir pinned a notice on the board saying that flour and energy cost more, so the loaf would cost a little more from Monday.

quiz.question: Which price stayed the same?
options: The price of the smaller roll
The price of every loaf
The price of the flour delivery
The price written in last year's book
quiz.correctAnswer: The price of the smaller roll
quiz.explanation: The notice promised that the smaller roll would stay the same price.
quiz.supportingSentence: The notice also promised that the smaller roll would stay the same price, so a tight budget still had an option.

quiz.question: Why was the cheaper item left unchanged?
options: Someone with little money would still have a choice
The loaf could then be removed from sale
Regulars would stop buying bread altogether
The record book could hide the change
quiz.correctAnswer: Someone with little money would still have a choice
quiz.explanation: The roll stayed the same price so a tight budget still had an option.
quiz.supportingSentence: The notice also promised that the smaller roll would stay the same price, so a tight budget still had an option.

quiz.question: What did the unhappy customer do on Friday?
options: She bought her usual loaves and accepted the new price
She stopped buying bread after reading the board
She took rolls only and left the loaves
She asked Samir to hide the new price
quiz.correctAnswer: She bought her usual loaves and accepted the new price
quiz.explanation: The customer who had grumbled said the bread was worth the new price and bought her usual two loaves.
quiz.supportingSentence: On Friday the customer who had grumbled said the bread was worth the new price and bought her usual two loaves.

quiz.question: What does grumbled mean in this story?
options: Complained in an unhappy way
Paid a higher price gladly
Wrote a figure in the money records
Changed from one bread to another
quiz.explanation: Regulars grumbled, and one said she might buy less often, so they were complaining.
quiz.supportingSentence: A few regulars grumbled, and one said she might buy bread less often.
